messages:
alex_k: Heads-up — profiler (dev-cluster) shows kernel chooser preferring cuBLASLt for medium seqs (256–512) + batch 8. That path requests ~220MB workspace vs Flash's ~120MB and we see +15% latency and higher OOM pressure. :eyes:

maria: Can you paste the kernel selection trace and the workspace numbers?

alex_k: sure, snippet from trace:
```
kernel_choice: cuBLASLt
workspace_requested: 220MB
flash_required: 120MB
runtime_policy: prefer_precise_workspace
```

kevin_t: Our current ws heuristic does `ws = ceil(seq/64)*base_slab` which overestimates when padding is common. That pushes Flash out since Flash needs smaller but more precisely sized buffers.

jenna: short proposal: compute per-kernel exact workspace for the current (batch, seq distribution) and pick kernel by estimated latency + workspace penalty. Pseudocode: 
```
for k in kernels:
  ws = k.workspace(batch, seq)
  est = k.latency_model(batch, seq, ws)
choose argmin(est + alpha*ws)
```
alpha is a tunable that converts bytes->latency/cost.

samuel: ran a small A/B with bump allocator + per-stream pool + dynamic kernel-sizing: median latency -7%, GPU memory -12% on average. BUT saw a regression for batch=1 seq=1024: latency +9ms and slight mem increase.

alex_k: logs from the run:
```
before: mem_used=11234MiB, p50=78ms
after : mem_used=9850MiB,  p50=73ms
regress(batch=1,seq=1024): mem_used=11400MiB, p50=87ms
```

maria: hmm fragmentation? how are frees merged?

kevin_t: we implemented free-on-complete per stream, but global merging of free-lists only every 100ms. Short bursts of big allocations (long seq singletons) can cause temporary fragmentation and force the chooser to pick a bigger-workspace kernel.

jenna: quick mitigation ideas: 1) immediate reclaim when a freed block > X bytes (return to global pool) 2) adaptive slab sizes: power-of-two for small slabs, exact sizing once >64MB 3) allow Flash/Triton kernels to request an overcommit hint so allocator can reserve contiguous sub-slab.

alex_k: also KV cache interaction: long sequential requests pin lots of KV pages; if we reuse prefix KV we should evict tail KV pages that haven't been hit. Otherwise allocator fragmentation + pinned KV = regression.

samuel: perf-bot fired yesterday on this:
```
perf-bot: alert model=gpt-lite-v2 region=prod-eu batch=1 seq=1024 p95 +18%  (since allocator patch)
```

maria: rollout plan suggestion: canary the allocator changes with per-route gating and add these console traces: `kernel_choice`, `workspace_bytes`, `allocator_frag_pct`, `kv_pinned_bytes`. We'll need histogram buckets for seq and batch.

kevin_t: i'll land the allocator change: immediate-large-free + merge-on-free-size threshold + unit tests that validate reuse and fragmentation scenarios.

jenna: i'll add exact-workspace calc for Flash/Triton/cuBLASLt + latency model lookup. We should also include a small fallback: if kernel_choice causes >X% mem spike compared to baseline, fallback to alternative kernel. That avoids long regressions in canary.

alex_k: plan summary: 1) exact workspace calc for all kernels 2) adaptive slab sizing 3) immediate reclamation for large frees 4) KV-tail eviction heuristic 5) canary with detailed traces + rollback gating.

maria: I can own the canary dashboards and SLO thresholds. Will add a Canary run tomorrow 03:00 UTC and a short smoke that includes batch=1 seq=1024 synthetic traffic.

infra-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-03-18T03:00Z on canary-cluster-2 (2h window). :white_check_mark:

samuel: one more note — we should be careful with the quantization/precision kernels: cuBLASLt may be chosen because its latency model picks up lower compute time even with higher ws. Tune alpha in the cost function accordingly.

alex_k: agreed. we'll keep alpha gated by customer tier (dedicated vs hosted) too. Thanks all — i'll follow up with PR links shortly. :thumbsup:
